propositions: Bridge git delivery abandons converged reconciliation after a single transient transport fault (TLS, DNS, timeout) instead of retrying, leaving unpushed commits orphaned on the runner.
The push.py retry classifier treats all non-fast-forward push failures identically, giving zero retries to transport faults while reserving retries only for genuine non-fast-forward conflicts.

Transport faults (certificate verification, connection reset, git timeout after 30s, promisor fetch failure) are incorrectly classified as terminal like policy violations, though transport faults are transient and retriable while policy violations are permanent.
The merge recovery leg in _merge_remote_under_lock fails terminally with merge-recovery-blocked on transport faults during promisor on-demand fetch in blob:none partial clones, without retry.
Current implementation lacks backoff or bounded retry budget for transport failures, creating risk of retry loops that cannot converge if a failure persists.
